rederived.value: Series H: $65B raised at $965B post-money ($900B pre-money, arithmetic and The Information); led by Altimeter, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, Sequoia; co-led by Capital Group, Coatue, D1, GIC, ICONIQ, XN; announced 2026-05-28. Includes $15B of previously committed hyperscaler money (incl. $5B Amazon). Prior round ~$380B (Series G, Feb 2026), not independently opened.

Latest MEASURED run-rate: >$65B annualized at end of July 2026 (reported 2026-08-17 by Bloomberg/TechCrunch, CNBC 'confirmed'; prior >$47B mid-May, company-stated in Series H post). A >$100B figure (NYT/Bloomberg/Axios, 2026-09-18) is an expectation for 2026 ('expected to generate more than $100B in annualized revenue this year'), not a measured run-rate. Bloomberg/TechCrunch first, CNBC 'confirmed' and Reuters 'source says', all from the same investor update (one update, several confirming people). Basis is GROSS: Anthropic books full marketplace sales, partner cut as expense (Axios 2026-09-03; CTech/Reuters 2026-09-30). The Axios Sep 18 'now pacing' wording cites the NYT as its source (Axios via Yahoo Finance, opened), so the $100B+ claim is one origin (NYT), and it is a projection.

FY2025 (calendar 2025) revenue ~$4.6B (nearly $4.6B; $4.59B in one report), ~12x FY2024 (~$0.38-0.40B implied); FY2025 operating loss ~$8.06B; net loss ~$42B incl. ~$34B non-cash charge; compute/infrastructure spend $7.33B. Basis: reported by Reuters (exclusive, 2026-09-28) and FT from a CONFIDENTIAL/LEAKED DRAFT prospectus (261 pages); NOT a public S-1 on EDGAR. Revenue is booked gross of cloud-partner fees ($351M distribution fees on $2.16B marketplace sales = 7.6% of revenue).

Confidential draft registration statement submitted and announced by Anthropic 2026-06-01; NO public S-1 on EDGAR as of 2026-09-30 (EDGAR company search: no match; press: 'not yet made public on SEC EDGAR'); draft prospectus leaked to Reuters/FT 2026-09-28. Reported target: raise up to ~$100B at ~$2T+ valuation (bankers to investors, NYT 2026-08-21; WSJ 2026-09-18). Timing: delayed from October to NOVEMBER 2026 (WSJ 2026-09-18, to show Q3 results). Exchange: Nasdaq (Bloomberg 2026-09-13, 'person familiar'). No price range, no share count.

Total compute/infrastructure commitments in the draft prospectus: at least $518B over ~10 years with six partners; ~80% ($~414B) non-cancelable or payable regardless of use (so ~$104B is not firm). Named: Google $111.1B, Amazon $110B (>$100B AWS over a decade), Microsoft $31.4B, Broadcom $161.2B (equipment leases), SpaceX $84.5B (earlier reported 'up to ~$45B'). Independent aggregate of announced deals: $517B (The Information, 2026-09-06). GW: no single disclosed total; aggregate of announcements is ~14-15 GW+ (Amazon+Google ~11 GW, Microsoft ~1 GW, AMD 2 GW, plus SpaceX/neoclouds); Series H post adds 5 GW Amazon and 5 GW Google/Broadcom TPU. 'Up to' items: Akamai $11.6B firm / ~$20B possible; Amazon investment up to $33B.

Most recent reported GM is basis-dependent and the two figures are NOT comparable: (a) FY2025 gross margin ~40% (Reuters Breakingviews 2026-09-29, from the prospectus; snippet only); (b) 2026 company-adjusted gross margin 'above 80%' BEFORE revenue shared with distribution partners and BEFORE model-training costs (FT 2026-09-13/14, relayed by TNW 2026-09-15). A PitchBook analyst estimate of 44% is circulating (MSN 2026-09-01). No audited 2026 GM exists.

NO public 'equalization ruling' found (Google News RSS, Bing News RSS, 1 WebSearch). The only sourced net-vs-gross adjustment is small: Axios 2026-09-03 (unnamed source) says moving Anthropic to a net basis 'would only amount to about a 6%-10% hit'; the draft prospectus gives $351M cloud-partner distribution fees on ~$4.6B FY2025 revenue = 7.6% (Reuters/CTech 2026-09-29/30). I found nothing supporting a 39.75% haircut; it cannot be sourced by me.

Bartz v. Anthropic PBC (N.D. Cal., 3:24-cv-05417): $1.5B class settlement (~$3,000 per work, ~500,000 works); final approval granted 2026-07-20 (Monday) by Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin per the settlement administrator site; press dated 2026-07-20/21. Fee award cut (~$101.6M). First payments expected on or before 2026-11-15.
